ownRead.title: Examples: from shapes to the next step
ownRead.description: Begin with string and water, then follow first structures, molecules, carbon arrangements, stars, cells, life and the brain.
ownRead.scope: An illustrative beginner explanation mapped to the original supplied RRG documents.
ownRead.body:
A string shows which motions fit a shape. Water lets you follow a moving pattern. Then the ladder follows first lasting structures, molecules, carbon arrangements, stars, cells, life changing its surroundings and the brain. This is a reading order; the carbon example compares arrangements along the way.

Each example follows the same questions: what happens, how RRG reads it, which rules and outward roles you can see, and where that reading stops. The mechanisms differ; the shared pattern is RRG’s proposal.

Read the examples in the order listed above, or use the [glossary](/glossary/) when a term is new. For the connected story, [read Start](/start/). [Background and new possibilities](/concepts/background/) follows how surroundings change what can form next.

Questions or ideas? [Contact the author](/contact/).
ownRead.sourceMapping: Editorial index of the nine illustrations, ordered with Contents. RRG v0.3.2 01 §§0–2: name-rules and string; §§5–7.2: molecules, separate roles and stellar ancestry; §§9–11: spreading, life and the brain; Observable Ladder addendum: early structures. Each new reading keeps its approved draft mapping. Unchanged core §§1–9 supplies the explanatory terms; each example retains its own source mapping and citations.
